1cWbOCeKHtUOqok2wexo8B9_Mq8RKO2wwiYDXETo.title: He Carried the Burning Bomb
lines: He carried a burning bomb with his bare hands, even though it had already blinded him,
you see, during a bombing mission over Japan, a smoke bomb exploded inside his plane and struck him in the face,
and smoke filled the cockpit until the pilot couldn’t see anything,
but then the plane began diving,
so he grabbed the burning bomb,
and with his hands burning, he struggled forward until he found the window and threw the bomb outside,
clearing the smoke from the plane helping the pilot save the plane from crashing into the ground!

15yC8hY0NL7jf-YkHKz5lVeqrMhLHW8zehpC3GYl.title: Can a Silencer Really Hide a Gunshot?
lines: If a soldier fires a gun with a silencer, could someone standing nearby really miss the shot,
you see, movies often turn the sound into a tiny puff, letting someone fire without anyone around them noticing,
and a real silencer does reduce the blast from the hot gas rushing out behind the bullet,
but that gas isn’t the only thing making noise,
because if the bullet travels faster than sound, it creates a sharp crack as it flies through the air,
and that sound happens outside the gun, after the bullet has already left the silencer,
so even with the blast reduced, the bullet itself can still give the shot away

1c0EydzIdnYBF3bE0ELWszPr627I082de3VuSIqM.title: He Fired From the Burning Ship
lines: This sailor kept firing from a burning cargo ship, even after an explosion left nobody at its main gun to fight back,
you see, German ships had caught them at sea and opened fire,
so the crew fired back, but a shell destroyed their boilers, leaving the ship unable to move,
and as the Germans kept hitting them, another shell exploded beside the main gun, knocking its wounded commander to the deck,
but this sailor ran to the gun and began loading and firing it himself,
until he had fired five more shells from the burning ship,
and although his own ship went down, the crew had damaged the German attacker so badly that it sank too

1hrRb5XoTtmqHcGQnzGUdeN_aM6bbkOPLYG_Vw4h.title: Their Last Torpedo Turned Back
lines: This submarine fired its last torpedo at the enemy, but it turned around and came straight back at them,
you see, the crew was trying to sink a Japanese ship,
so they fired the first torpedo and watched it head toward the target,
but when they launched the second, it curved sharply instead of going straight, circling back toward their submarine,
so the crew pushed the engines to emergency speed and tried to turn out of its path,
until their own torpedo struck near the back of the submarine and sent it sinking.

1CUoRRCFu0kCRGK0ILDjg5DB3m7ftY_DZklxIOtW.title: He Told His Own Guns to Fire on Him
lines: He ordered his own men to fire directly at him,
you see, his men were pulling out of a village under attack, but he stayed behind in a building to tell the artillery where to shoot,
and as the Germans advanced through the streets, he kept calling the explosions closer,
but they kept advancing until they surrounded the building,
so he told the guns to fire on his position,
and when his commander warned that the shells would land on him, he insisted they fire anyway,
until the bombardment killed him and the men who had stayed beside him,
and more than fifty years later, his wife received the Medal of Honor on his behalf

15zx17oq2TLGcx1q1g1vhtHnI-0Pl4LrfrMPzVO3.title: He Pulled the Second Grenade Under Him
lines: This teenage Marine threw himself onto a live grenade, then pulled a second one under his body so neither could explode beside his friends,
you see, he was fighting on Iwo Jima when the grenades landed in the trench he shared with three other Marines,
so he pushed one man aside, dropped onto the grenades and pressed them into the dirt beneath him,
until one exploded, throwing him onto his back and filling his body with metal,
and believing he was dead, his friends continued the attack, leaving him behind,
but he was still conscious, struggling to breathe and unable to call for help,
until a passing Marine spotted him and called a medic,
and despite taking the blast against his own body, he survived, along with the three men he had shielded

1BSad0XTzDJwHeshbYlJW1ms3WOXcJloW-ClCn7u.title: The Medic Who Stayed on Hacksaw Ridge
lines: When Japanese fire drove American soldiers off a ridge on Okinawa, an unarmed medic named Desmond Doss stayed at the top with the men who were too badly wounded to follow,
and with the wounded still exposed to gunfire, Doss carried them one at a time to the edge of the cliff,
where he lowered each man on a stretcher tied to a rope until the soldiers below could take him,
and every time they took a man off the stretcher, Doss could pull it back up and go looking for another,
until that one medic had lowered about 75 men to safety

1cIuKnWP6294pkYdOmQk9KWwqitAW2B3VipE5FSO.title: The Ship That Was Still a Bomb
lines: This captain deliberately crashed his ship into a German-held dock, with tons of explosives hidden inside,
you see, the British wanted to destroy the dock so Germany’s biggest battleship couldn’t be repaired there,
so after smashing into its gates, the crew abandoned the ship, leaving the explosives set to go off later,
but the explosion never happened,
so German soldiers climbed aboard the wreck, searching through it and even collecting souvenirs,
but while they searched tthe ship suddenly exploded, tearing the gates apart and leaving the dock unusable for the rest of the war

1QZgZEcfKDQvg_4E2GepoPevo187NHn5nvdnuIST.title: Version 2 — They Thought He Had Failed
lines: A German officer mocked this captured captain for crashing his ship into a dock, without knowing the ship was still waiting to explode,
you see, the British had hidden tons of explosives inside it, then rammed it into the gates of a dock where Germany’s biggest battleship could be repaired,
and after the crew abandoned the wreck, the explosives were supposed to blow the gates apart,
but the time passed, and nothing happened,
so German soldiers began climbing aboard, searching the ship and taking souvenirs, while the explosives remained hidden inside,
and as the officer questioned the captain, he told him that crashing a ship could never destroy such enormous gates,
until the whole harbor shook, as the explosives finally went off, destroying the gates and leaving the dock unusable for the rest of the war

1trCGkbS_4V8c9JRCYaleJU3rwgXxAavj3Va1lSc.title: Version 1 — Will They Find the Bomb?
lines: The captain crashed a ship packed with explosives into a German-held dock, but the explosives didn’t go off when they were supposed to,
you see the British needed to destroy the dock so Germany’s biggest battleship couldn’t be repaired,
so the crew destroyed the gates and abandoned the ship, leaving the explosives hidden inside,
but hours passed without any explosion, so German soldiers climbed aboard and began searching the wreck,
and while the soldiers even started collecting souvenirs,
the bomb exploded destroying the gates, putting the dock out of action for the rest of the war

1Tsr5MKNPygSzDfJ4NvDtZXJQ5AofKN8qePwTFxb.title: Their Own Torpedo Turned Back
lines: This submarine fired its last torpedo at an enemy ship, but then the torpedo turned around and came straight back at them,
you see, the crew had already damaged a Japanese ship and were firing their final shots to finish it off,
but instead of continuing toward the target, the last torpedo curved through the water, bringing the submarine that had fired it directly into its path,
so the captain ordered emergency speed and tried to swing the submarine out of the way,
but before they could get clear, their own torpedo slammed into the back of the submarine and exploded,
just twenty seconds after they had fired it,
sending the submarine to the bottom, with only nine of its crew surviving

1PEhVBJRSEqB-dNSbMs8bjEfjLC3Wr_t0cvqeokX.title: Embed Nick’s scriptwriting feedback
lines: This wounded soldier told his friends to leave him behind with a pistol and eight bullets while the enemy closed in,
you see, Japanese troops were attacking from three sides, and he kept firing even after he was badly wounded,
until his ammunition ran out and his gun was smashed in the fighting,
and rather than let anyone else get hurt trying to save him, he asked to be propped against a tree,
and refused any kind of help while facing the attackers as his friends pulled back,
so when American troops returned, they found him dead against the same tree,
with the pistol empty and eight Japanese soldiers lying dead in front of him

1ID2z-n68McNbdw2tPb62q1dDeaPaKjoqYKux-Gk.title: He Put His Boat in Front of the Guns
lines: This man drove his small boat between Japanese guns and a beach full of trapped Marines, deliberately making himself the target,
you see, nearly five hundred Marines needed to escape by sea, but Japanese machine guns were firing as the rescue boats approached,
so he led the boats toward the beach and signalled the others to land,
then placed his own boat in front of the enemy fire, using its guns to cover the Marines as they climbed aboard,
but with the evacuation almost finished, he was hit and killed,
and two of his crew were wounded too,
yet the crew kept going until the last boat had loaded and cleared the beach, getting the Marines away while the man who shielded them never came home

1t1rBuh47mraUefL4CaL5VHkWHEHXfkXWx2ji8-R.title: Thirty Seconds to Get Out
lines: These men planted explosives inside a German-controlled factory, then gave themselves only thirty seconds to get clear,
you see, the British feared the factory could help Germany build an atomic bomb, so they sent Norwegian soldiers to wreck its equipment,
but the bridge was guarded, so the men climbed down into a deep valley, crossed an icy river and climbed up the other side,
then they cut through a fence, only to find the door into the building locked,
so two of them found a tunnel and crawled inside, where they placed explosives beside the equipment,
then they lit the short fuses and fled,
and the charges exploded, wrecking production for months, while every man on the raid escaped without being captured

1RPuYC-gg407TYJ8DBnInReooKQ-080KXipeQ8Dr.title: The Burning Ship That Could Not Turn Away
lines: This American warship was burning and stuck turning in circles, while Japanese pilots kept trying to crash their planes into it,
you see, the ship was watching for enemy aircraft off Okinawa when the attack began,
and although its gunners shot planes down, others smashed into the ship, spreading burning fuel across the deck,
then a bomb jammed its steering, so the crew could no longer turn where they wanted as more attackers came in,
but while sailors fought the fires, the guns that still worked kept firing,
and American fighters joined the battle overhead, helping stop more planes from reaching the wreck,
until the attack finally ended, and despite the fires, bombs and planes that had smashed into it, the ship stayed afloat and was towed to safety

1bXm8VOcglP2ink-USr0FvVGTCn14T4fN-f4fm8M.title: He Stole a Ship to Free His Family
lines: This enslaved man escaped with his family on a Confederate ship, but first he had to take them past forts that could sink it,
you see, when the officers went ashore for the night, he and the other enslaved crewmen took the ship and collected their families,
then he put on the captain’s coat and hat, while the women and children hid below deck,
and as the ship approached the forts, he gave the signals the guards expected, so they let it pass,
but when they reached a Union warship, its captain mistook them for an enemy coming to attack and prepared his guns,
so the crew hurried to raise a white bedsheet, showing they were surrendering,
and the ship pulled alongside with the families aboard finally free

1tL5Stkd1uSgUMOd4ggW0MCFIwdeIp0sI_tQ3OoD.title: He Went Back With Only a Knife
lines: This wounded soldier ran at the Germans carrying his friend away, even though his rifle had jammed and he had only a knife left,
you see, the two Americans were guarding an outpost at night when a German raiding party attacked and wounded them both,
and as his badly injured friend was being carried off, he tried to reload, but his gun would no longer fire,
so he swung it at an attacker, knocked him down, then drew his knife and went after the men taking his friend,
but the soldier he had knocked down got back up and wounded him again,
and even then he kept fighting, until the Germans finally retreated, leaving his friend behind alive

1ZI3-w7VLwHieS5jqKXQIH0bvRzTze_GQpPJhPk6.title: Your rules prompt: draft for review
lines: Return status (ready_for_editor, needs_review or needs_research), narration_lines, claim_map, unresolved_issues and a short editorial_reason. If you have any doubt about a fact, the status is not ready_for_editor. ready_for_editor means ready for Nick to read, not approved. [src: v1]

1Mzicch8UL5OLrhU12qxEPR1mKpxwOb2_Gm0sdMh.title: Blind test: the two Neither stories
lines: Both stories below got Neither in the blind test. Edit, cut, comment freely: your changes are the feedback. The originals are saved separately.
Story 1: The War Started And Ended At His House 🏠
Pitch: After the first big battle of the Civil War wrecked his farm, a man moved his family 120 miles away to a sleepy village so the war could never find him again.
Script 1 (v1 plus your rules, 147 words)
A Union shell smashed through a Virginia man's kitchen and into the dinner of the Confederate officers inside,
because Wilmer McLean's farm near Bull Run had become their general's headquarters on the eve of the war's first big battle,
Two years later he moved his family south to Appomattox, near a railroad for his sugar business and far from the fighting,
but in 1865 the war found him again,
when Robert E. Lee's aide rode into town looking for a place to meet Grant, and ran into McLean, who first suggested an empty tavern,
and when the aide turned it down, the meeting moved into McLean's own parlor,
where Lee surrendered to Grant,
after which Union officers bought or carried off his furniture as souvenirs, even a child's doll,
McLean supposedly summed it up: the war began in his front yard and ended in his front parlor.
Script 2 (v1 as written, 149 words)
In 1861, a Union shell crashed through the kitchen of a Virginia farm and ruined the Confederate officers' dinner,
the farm belonged to Wilmer McLean, whose house was General Beauregard's headquarters during the war's first big battle,
and later, McLean moved his family about 120 miles south to a village called Appomattox, near a railroad for his sugar business and far from the fighting,
but in April 1865, an aide to General Lee rode into the village looking for a place where Lee could meet General Grant, and ran into McLean,
who first suggested an empty tavern, but the aide turned it down, so the meeting ended up in McLean's own parlor,
where Lee surrendered to Grant, who gave him generous terms,
then Union officers carried off his tables and chairs as souvenirs,
and two years later, unable to pay his mortgage, McLean sold the house where Lee surrendered.
Story 2: The Night Out That Almost Started WW3 🎭
Pitch: An American diplomat just wanted to see a play in East Berlin, but a guard asked for his ID, and within days American and Soviet tanks were aiming at each other from 100 yards apart.
Script 1 (v1 as written, 149 words)
An American diplomat was heading to a show in East Berlin when East German guards at Checkpoint Charlie demanded his papers.
But he refused, because Allied forces could move freely across Berlin, and he insisted only the Soviets could check him,
so General Clay began sending Americans across under armed escort, and US tanks rolled up to the checkpoint.
Khrushchev ordered his forces to match them tank for tank, and late one afternoon ten Soviet tanks faced ten American tanks about 100 yards apart, their guns trained on each other.
When Kennedy phoned Clay and told him not to lose his nerve, Clay said it was Washington's nerves he worried about,
and the next morning the Soviet tanks began backing away, for reasons no record has settled, and the American tanks followed,
and the US stopped the escorts, ending a standoff that began with a trip to a show.
Script 2 (v1 plus your rules, 132 words)
An American diplomat was driving to a show in East Berlin when East German guards at Checkpoint Charlie demanded his papers,
but he refused, saying the Allies could move freely anywhere in Berlin and only the Soviets could check him,
so armed military police began escorting officials across, then an American general made the escorts bigger, determined to win back America's standing in the city,
and when American tanks rolled up to the checkpoint, Soviet leader Khrushchev ordered his army to match them tank for tank,
leaving Soviet and American tanks facing off through the night, their main guns aimed at one another.
But the next morning one Soviet tank backed up, an American tank followed, and one by one they all pulled away,
and soon after, America stopped the armed escorts.

1hb5FohY1C_Omgv7hK1YXbxm18SGAMeZMcxquvjN.title: The SEAL Who Went Back
lines: He ran back to the middle of the battlefield to save his lieutenant from enemy gunfire. (highest stake in story becomes the hook - so the hook IS the foreshadow.)
You see, when **Michael Thornton landed**  by mistake deep inside North Vietnam,
a gunfight broke out bringing dozens of enemy soldiers running towards them,
so his lieutenant called their own warship to shell the beach, and stayed behind to hold the soldiers off, but instantly got a bullet in the head
leaving him unconscious right where the shells were about to land,
so Thornton turned around and ran back through the gunfire, but just as he reached the lieutenant  the shells hit the beach
throwing both men far into the air and giving Thornton time to swim out to sea escaping from the enemy and finally reaching their boat.
(script ends at the cliffhanger of what happened to the lieutenant which will get people asking in the comments what happened)

1co32HGlMPmKAtONbEveF_r2TTi6dm-PpwDwS9OB.title: The Invasion Of The Empty Island
lines: Almost 40,000 American and Canadian soldiers landed on an island and started shooting into fog so thick they couldn't see ten feet ahead.
You see, Japanese troops had stormed the island of Kiska and captured the small American weather station there,
so over a year later, the Americans and Canadians came to take it back,
where a Canadian soldier opened fire, sure the men in front of him were Japanese,
starting a fight in the fog that killed 28 Americans and 4 Canadians,
but there were no Japanese left to fight,

since weeks earlier, when the American ships guarding the island pulled back to refuel, Japanese ships hidden by the fog slipped into the harbor and carried over 5,000 men away in about fifty minutes,
yet even after the island's radio went silent, American warships and planes kept pounding it for weeks,
and as the troops searched the island, all they found were a few dogs and the booby traps the Japanese had left behind, which killed more of them,
so taking an island with no enemy on it cost 92 Allied lives.

1L0o3xzjpvGCqDPnTPYTkg3hfCf346ofq7oVydsA.title: The Captain Who Saved His Enemies
lines: Japanese captain Shunsaku Kudo stopped his warship in waters where enemy submarines and planes were lurking, beside hundreds of British and American sailors his own navy had sunk the day before,
because they had been drifting for about 20 hours, clinging to rafts and floats, many so coated in oil they couldn't see,
and since he respected the British navy, he couldn't leave them there,
so he sent almost his whole crew to pull them aboard with rope ladders and bamboo poles, keeping only the gunners of his front turret ready to fight,
until his ship was carrying more than 400 enemy sailors against his own crew of about 220, too crowded to fight back if a submarine struck,
where Kudo told the British officers in English, 'You have fought bravely. Now you are the honoured guests of the Imperial Japanese Navy,'
but he never spoke of it to anyone, not even his family,
so they only learned what he had done after he died, when one of the men he had saved came looking for his grave.

1qviYhcvlyWDrumGUs7Ki8zg56Zd5A81PhGgCxgH.title: The Pig That Almost Started A War
lines: An American farmer shot a pig that belonged to a British company when it was caught digging up his potatoes,
But when the farmer refused to pay for it the British threatened to arrest him,
leading the Americans on the island to beg the US Army for protection, which sent soldiers who swore to fight to the last man if attacked,
and since Britain saw armed American troops on an island it claimed, it then sent warships to remove them,
putting both sides one order away from war,
but the British admiral in charge refused to attack, saying he would not involve two great nations in a war over a squabble about a pig,
so both sides pulled most of their troops out and shared the island for 12 years,
leaving the pig as the only casualty of the entire standoff.

14JqrUFPjpZMK_nEg7nqN5SNyjPaKZSiWBU9JwyH.title: No Shooting On Christmas Eve
lines: I was a 12-year-old German boy hiding with my mother in a cabin ~~deep in the forest near the Belgian border~~ **in the forest** , while one of the biggest battles of the war raged around us.
And on Christmas Eve, when three armed American soldiers knocked on our door, one of them shot in the leg ~~and lying in the snow~~ , my mother let them in.
But I was ~~almost paralyzed with fear~~ **terrified** , because hiding enemy soldiers counted as treason, and it could get ~~everyone in our house~~ **us all**  executed.
Then, while she was treating ~~their frozen feet and fingers~~ **them** , there was another knock.
It was four German soldiers ~~who had lost their unit and were asking~~ **lost and asking**  for shelter.
And the moment they ~~stepped inside and~~  saw the Americans, their leader started to object.
But my mother looked at him and said, 'It is the Holy Night, and there will be no shooting here.'

So the Germans ~~piled their pistols, rifles, a machine gun and two bazookas on the woodpile, the Americans gave up their weapons too,~~ **laid down their weapons, the Americans did the same,**  and one of the Germans, who had studied medicine, checked the wounded American's leg ~~and found the cold had kept it from getting infected~~ .

Since our one rooster wasn't enough to feed everyone, my mother cooked it into a soup ~~with potatoes and oats, the Germans added red wine and bread,~~  and when she said grace, some of the soldiers cried.

The next morning, ~~after my mother gave up her best tablecloth to make a stretcher,~~  the German leader used the Americans' map to show them the way back to their troops, gave them a compass, ~~and once my mother handed back everyone's weapons,~~  they shook hands and walked off in opposite directions.
For the next 50 years, I had no idea if any of those soldiers made it home.

But after a TV show told our story, ~~a chaplain in America called in about an old soldier named Ralph Blank, and when I finally met him, he was 76 and sick,~~ **I finally met one of the Americans, who**  still had the German compass and map, and told me ~~five~~ **four**  words.
Your mother saved my life.
My mother never got to hear it, because she had died 30 years earlier.

1hP3Ej8XXiEFVd7U1VFk6YH3YtsEI9UowIwQJqhs.title: The Captain Who Sank His Own Ship
lines: A German captain sank nine British cargo ships without killing a single person, and whenever he took a crew prisoner, he welcomed them and apologized for sinking their ship.

But when some British warships hit his ship about 70 times, he ended up limping into a port in Uruguay, where he was told he had only 72 hours to leave, **while the British sent fake radio messages**  that a huge fleet with an aircraft carrier was waiting outside to seize his ship but since **it carried Germany's secret new radar**  there was no way he would let them take it**,**
So instead of giving up his country’s secrets he detonated **explosives he had planted on board,**  which tore the ship apart**,**
**And since** **he couldn't bear anyone thinking he sank his ship to save his own life, three days later he shot himself .**
